PEP 20 – The Zen of Python Author:Tim Peters <tim.peters at gmail.com>Status:Active Type:Informational Created:19-Aug-2004 Post-History:22-Aug-2004

* * *

Table of Contents

## [Abstract](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/#abstract)

Long time Pythoneer Tim Peters succinctly channels the BDFL’s guiding principles for Python’s design into 20 aphorisms, only 19 of which have been written down.

## [The Zen of Python](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/#the-zen-of-python)

Beautiful is better than ugly.
Explicit is better than implicit.
Simple is better than complex.
Complex is better than complicated.
Flat is better than nested.
Sparse is better than dense.
Readability counts.
Special cases aren't special enough to break the rules.
Although practicality beats purity.
Errors should never pass silently.
Unless explicitly silenced.
In the face of ambiguity, refuse the temptation to guess.
There should be one-- and preferably only one --obvious way to do it.
Although that way may not be obvious at first unless you're Dutch.
Now is better than never.
Although never is often better than *right* now.
If the implementation is hard to explain, it's a bad idea.
If the implementation is easy to explain, it may be a good idea.
Namespaces are one honking great idea -- let's do more of those!

## [Easter Egg](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/#easter-egg)

>>> import this

## [References](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/#references)

Originally posted to [comp.lang.python/python-list@python.org](mailto:comp.lang.python/python-list%40python.org) under a thread called [“The Way of Python”](https://groups.google.com/d/msg/comp.lang.python/B_VxeTBClM0/L8W9KlsiriUJ)

# 🌐 超大 KG（个人知识总图）

> **触发关键词**：说 "**超大KG**" + 一段 LLM 解释 → 自动调用 `super-kg` skill 分类保存。
> 
> **说明**：这是一个层级化的知识图谱，从宏观领域 → 细分赛道 → 具体问题 → 局部细节，逐层下钻。  
> **原则**：LLM 的详细解释**全文保留，一字不改**，用 `> [!quote]-` 折叠装载；骨架本身也可点击标题折叠。

---

## 📖 使用说明（折叠 / 展开机制）

> [!info]- 点击展开「如何使用本文档」
> 
> ### 三层折叠机制
> 
> | 层级 | 折叠方式 | 默认状态 |
> |------|---------|---------|
> | **标题（H2/H3/H4/H5）** | 鼠标悬停标题，点击左侧三角形 | 展开 |
> | **Callout `[!quote]-`** | 点击 callout 标题行 | **默认折叠** ✓ |
> | **Callout `[!quote]+`** | 点击 callout 标题行 | 默认展开 |
> 
> ### 层级约定
> 
> ```
> H2 (##)   一级领域       — 例：🧠 AI & 机器学习
>   H3 (###)   二级方向      — 例：大语言模型 (LLM)
>     H4 (####)   子赛道       — 例：检索增强生成 (RAG)
>       H5 (#####)   具体问题    — 例：KG 路径推理的本质
>         > [!quote]- 子问题标题  — 装 LLM 原文（默认折叠）
> ```
> 
> ### 录入新条目的格式
> 
> ````markdown
> ##### 具体问题标题
> 
> > [!quote]- 简短摘要标题（YYYY-MM-DD）
> > 
> > **来源**：[对话来源 / LLM 模型]  
> > **关联**：[[相关笔记]] / #tag
> > 
> > ---
> > 
> > [LLM 原文，一字不改]
> ````
> 
> ### 给 Claude 的指令模板
> 
> > "保存这段到知识图谱：[粘贴 LLM 原文]"  
> > → Claude 自动判断 L1/L2/L3/L4 位置，追加 `[!quote]-` 折叠块

---

## 🤖 自适应机制（Claude 工作准则）

> [!important]- 点击展开「Claude 每次录入和重组的标准流程」
> 
> ### Step 1: 录入前必做（每次都要）
> 
> 1. **读骨架**：先读 `_meta/骨架.json`，了解现有层级
> 2. **读现状**：跑 `python scripts/kg_status.py` 看各节点条目数
> 3. **匹配判断**：
>    - 匹配度 **> 0.7** → 直接归入最匹配的 L5 节点
>    - 匹配度 **0.4–0.7** → 反问用户："倾向 A 还是 B？"
>    - 匹配度 **< 0.4** → 暂存到 `📌 待分类（暂存区）`，标注主题词
> 
> ### Step 2: 录入时
> 
> 1. 找到合适 H5（没有就新建 H5）
> 2. 追加 `> [!quote]- 简短标题（日期）` 折叠块
> 3. 原文**一字不改**
> 4. 同步更新 `_meta/骨架.json` 中该路径下的条目数组
> 
> ### Step 3: 录入后必做（阈值监控）
> 
> 1. 跑 `python scripts/kg_status.py --rebalance`
> 2. 若有节点超阈值 → **主动提示用户**重组建议（不要等用户问）
> 3. 用户确认后执行重组
> 
> ### Step 4: 自适应重组规则
> 
> | 触发条件 | 建议动作 |
> |---------|---------|
> | L5 quotes > 5 | 拆出 L6 子问题 |
> | L4 下 L5 子节点 > 15 | 拆出更多 L5 分组 |
> | L3 下 L4 子赛道 > 30 | 拆出更多 L4 分组 |
> | L2 总条目 > 80 | 独立成单独 md 文件 |
> | 相邻 L4 各 ≤ 2 条且主题相似 | 合并 |
> | L3 整个 < 3 条 | 上移合并到 L2 |
> 
> ### Step 5: 待分类区清理
> 
> - 每积累 5 条以上，主动建议归位
> - 找出共同主题，建议归到现有 L3/L4 或新建分支
> 
> ### Step 6: 操作日志
> 
> 每次重组都在 `_meta/重组日志.md` 追加一条记录（时间、动作、影响节点）。
>

citations.preview:
In the following examples, input and output are distinguished by the presence or absence of prompts ([>>>](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-0) and […](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-...)): to repeat the example, you must type everything after the prompt, when the prompt appears; lines that do not begin with a prompt are output from the interpreter. Note that a secondary prompt on a line by itself in an example means you must type a blank line; this is used to end a multi-line command.

You can use the “Copy” button (it appears in the upper-right corner when hovering over or tapping a code example), which strips prompts and omits output, to copy and paste the input lines into your interpreter.

Many of the examples in this manual, even those entered at the interactive prompt, include comments. Comments in Python start with the hash character, `#`, and extend to the end of the physical line. A comment may appear at the start of a line or following whitespace or code, but not within a string literal. A hash character within a string literal is just a hash character. Since comments are to clarify code and are not interpreted by Python, they may be omitted when typing in examples.

Some examples:

# this is the first comment
spam = 1  # and this is the second comment
          # ... and now a third!
text = "# This is not a comment because it's inside quotes."

## 3.1. Using Python as a Calculator[¶](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/introduction.html#using-python-as-a-calculator "Link to this heading")

Let’s try some simple Python commands. Start the interpreter and wait for the primary prompt, `>>>`. (It shouldn’t take long.)

### 3.1.1. Numbers[¶](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/introduction.html#numbers "Link to this heading")

The interpreter acts as a simple calculator: you can type an expression into it and it will write the value. Expression syntax is straightforward: the operators `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` can be used to perform arithmetic; parentheses (`()`) can be used for grouping. For example:

>>> 2 + 2
4
>>> 50 - 5*6
20
>>> (50 - 5*6) / 4
5.0
>>> 8 / 5  # division always returns a floating-point number
1.6

The integer numbers (e.g. `2`, `4`, `20`) have type [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int "int"), the ones with a fractional part (e.g. `5.0`, `1.6`) have type [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/
